creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`rad check` reports an error on the `epoch` tutorial that `rad docs examples/epoch` ships. The corpus's most-used working script, `cct` at 1103 runs, carries 13 hints. Both review sources reached the same conclusion independently: users learn to skim the hint tier, and then the tier stops working.

Four confirmed false positives, all cases where the surrounding code proves the hint wrong:

- `read_file(...).content` types as `str|int[]` and isn't narrowed by the default `mode="text"`. `refineBuiltinReturn` is the extension point, but it currently sees only positional argument types, so narrowing on a literal kwarg needs literal-type tracking. Sites: `msh:240`, `peer:156`, `htree:182,199`.
- `index_of` returns `int?` and isn't narrowed by an `in` membership guard, so `idx + 1` fires RAD30002 on code that provably can't be null. Hit ~10 times in one script from a single `args.index_of(flag)` flag-parsing idiom.
- Lockstep `sort()` erases element types. It's declared `(_primary: list|str, *_others: list|str) -> list|str` because it sorts strings too, so a destructured capture keeps a `str` possibility that fails any `list`-typed parameter. Three-list capture reports `dynamic|null` instead. Single capture is clean and indexing is unaffected, so it's specifically builtins declaring `list`. The script that hit this kept an unsorted copy under a second name purely to satisfy the checker.
- `.map()` results type as `map|list` (`notes:30`); `[".."] + children` types as `str[] + list|str` (`zook:95`).

The #129 fix in v0.11.0 (`9d986d86`) shows the class is tractable.

This is also a precondition for the migration tooling. Nobody adopts `--fix` on the strength of a diagnostic tier they've been trained to ignore.

---

### Orientation

- All four false positives live in `rts/check/`, which owns the static checker. `rts` must not import `core`.
- Two extension points. `rts/check/type_check.go:2744` `refineBuiltinReturn` sharpens a builtin's declared return type for a specific call site. `rts/check/narrow.go` holds the flow-sensitive narrowing, keyed on Symbols in a Frame.
- Signatures are not written in Go. They come from `docs/funcs/*.md` via codegen into `rts/signatures_gen.go`, so a fix expressed as a narrower signature means editing markdown and running `make generate`.

### Watch out for

- `rts` must not import `core`.
- Signatures live in `docs/funcs/*.md`. If a fix is best expressed as a narrower signature, edit the markdown and run `make generate` - `rts/signatures_gen.go` is generated output.
- `refineBuiltinReturn` is conservative on purpose. Widening it wrongly makes the checker miss real errors, which is a worse failure than hint noise. Every refinement needs a matching negative snapshot case.
- The `index_of` item is a different size class from the other three. Landing three of four is a better outcome than stalling on the fourth; if it gets deferred, split it onto its own card rather than leaving this one open.
title: Stop the checker firing hints on provably-safe code
